project.name: Exasol Studio
project.description: Tauri 2 (Rust) + React 19 desktop client for Exasol databases with a Node agent-core AI sidecar, an ANTLR SQL parser, and a database-side semantic-views layer.

nodes.name: components.json
nodes.summary: shadcn/ui configuration for the desktop app, selecting the radix-nova style, lucide icon library, Tailwind CSS variables, and import aliases (@/components, @/lib, @/components/ui) plus magicui and ai-elements component registries.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives shadcn CLI code generation; aliases mirror the tsconfig path mapping.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the @exasol-studio/desktop Tauri app, declaring React 19, Tauri 2 plugins, Monaco/Perspective/Tiptap/xterm UI dependencies, the workspace SQL parser, and dev/build/tauri scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pnpm workspace protocol (workspace:*) to consume the local exasol-sql-parser package; type: module for ESM.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript compiler configuration for the desktop app, extending the workspace base config with react-jsx, Vite/Node types, the @/* path alias to ./src, and noEmit for type-check-only builds.
nodes.languageNotes: The @/* paths mapping mirrors the aliases declared in components.json.

nodes.name: acl-manifests.json
nodes.summary: Tauri-generated ACL permission manifests enumerating the available commands and permission scopes for core plugins (app, event, image, menu, path, resources, tray, webview, window) and the dialog, opener, process, and updater plugins.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated artifact under src-tauri/gen/schemas; defines per-plugin permission identifiers consumed by Tauri's capability system.

nodes.name: capabilities.json
nodes.summary: Tauri-generated capabilities manifest that maps the resolved 'default' capability set to the windows and permissions granted to the desktop application's webview.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated aggregation of capability definitions; the 'default' capability binds granted permissions to app windows.

nodes.name: desktop-schema.json
nodes.summary: Tauri-generated JSON Schema describing the valid structure of desktop capability configuration files, including permission definitions and window bindings.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON Schema with an anyOf top-level and a large definitions block; validates capability config authored for the desktop target.

nodes.name: macOS-schema.json
nodes.summary: Tauri-generated JSON Schema describing the valid structure of macOS-specific capability configuration files; mirrors the desktop schema for the macOS platform target.
nodes.languageNotes: Platform-specialized JSON Schema; structurally identical to desktop-schema.json, scoped to the macOS build target.

nodes.name: sales_databricks_metric_view.yaml
nodes.summary: Example Databricks Unity Catalog Metric View (UCMV) written over the demo MART tables, used to exercise and validate the SEMANTIC_ADMIN.IMPORT_DATABRICKS_METRIC_VIEW import path.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares source, joins, fields, and measures in Databricks UCMV YAML format so it compiles against the project's demo data.

nodes.name: sales_materializations.sql
nodes.summary: Creates the SALES_REVENUE_BY_REGION aggregate table and registers it as a manual materialization of the sales semantic model via SEMANTIC_ADMIN scripts.

nodes.name: SALES_REVENUE_BY_REGION
nodes.summary: Aggregate materialization table summing net revenue per customer region, joining order lines to orders and customers.

nodes.name: sales_metrics_semantic_definition.sql
nodes.summary: SQL-native semantic authoring example that alters the sales SEMANTIC VIEW to declare facts and metrics (net_revenue, net_cost, quantity), targeting the definition runtime and preprocessor surface.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the proposed Semantic SQL DDL (ALTER SEMANTIC VIEW ... REPLACE FACTS ...) rather than legacy SEMANTIC_ADMIN script calls.

nodes.name: sales_model_fixup.sql
nodes.summary: One-time maintenance script that corrects the order_quarter dimension expression and removes a test dimension artifact from a live sales semantic model, then re-runs validation.

nodes.name: sales_model_seed.sql
nodes.summary: Seeds the certified sales semantic model by invoking SEMANTIC_ADMIN scripts to create the model and register its entities, dimensions, and metrics over the MART tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Long sequence of EXECUTE SCRIPT SEMANTIC_ADMIN.* calls (CREATE_MODEL, ADD_ENTITY, ...) forming the reference smoke-seed for the semantic views feature.

nodes.name: sales_osi.yaml
nodes.summary: Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) export of the sales semantic model describing datasets, primary keys, and Exasol vendor custom extensions mapping to the MART source tables.

nodes.name: sales_physical_model.sql
nodes.summary: Physical star-schema DDL and seed data for the demo MART schema (customers, products, orders, order lines) that underlies the sales semantic model examples.

nodes.name: CUSTOMERS
nodes.summary: Customer dimension table keyed by CUSTOMER_ID with name and region attributes.

nodes.name: PRODUCTS
nodes.summary: Product dimension table keyed by PRODUCT_ID with product name and category.

nodes.name: ORDERS
nodes.summary: Order header table keyed by ORDER_ID referencing a customer, with order date and status.

nodes.name: ORDER_LINES
nodes.summary: Order line grain fact table (composite key ORDER_ID, LINE_ID) with quantity, net unit price, and unit cost measures.

nodes.name: sales_semantic_queries.sql
nodes.summary: Example read-only queries against the SEMANTIC_CATALOG views to inspect the sales model, its object columns, and registered metrics.

nodes.name: 000_create_schemas.sql
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the Exasol semantic-layer install by creating the SYS_SEMANTIC, SEMANTIC_CATALOG, SEMANTIC_ADMIN and SEMANTIC_AGENT schemas plus two discovery tables that advertise the catalog and agent surfaces.

nodes.name: 001_create_semantic_catalog.sql
nodes.summary: Defines the core SYS_SEMANTIC data model: 34 tables storing semantic models, versions, entities, objects, relationships, dimensions, facts, metrics, materializations, validation, agent and audit data.
nodes.languageNotes: Highly normalized relational model; version and audit columns (CREATED_AT/UPDATED_AT/BY) recur across most tables.

nodes.name: 003_create_semantic_admin_scripts.sql

tour.title: Monorepo Layout
tour.description: Start here to see the shape of the whole project. The root package.json pins pnpm and exposes repo-level scripts, while pnpm-workspace.yaml declares the two halves of the codebase you will tour: the apps/* desktop client and the packages/* libraries (agent-core sidecar and the SQL parser). Understanding this split up front makes it clear why the app, the AI agent, and the parser live and build separately yet ship as one product.

tour.title: React Frontend Boot
tour.description: This is where the user-facing app comes to life. main.tsx is the React entry point: it applies the saved theme preset and window-controls inset, then mounts App inside the ThemeProvider and TooltipProvider. App.tsx is the root component that composes the desktop UI shell and wires the top-level providers and routing. Together they are the 'how does the UI start?' answer that everything visual hangs off of.

tour.title: The Workbench Shell
tour.description: Building on the App shell from Step 2, ExasolStudio.tsx is the main workbench screen that assembles the title bar, sidebar, SQL editor tabs, results grid, history dock, and visualizer into the full database-client experience. DatabaseTree.tsx renders the hierarchical explorer of schemas, tables, and objects that lives in that sidebar. This is the screen a user actually spends their day in.

tour.title: The IPC Bridge
tour.description: The frontend never talks to a database directly — it goes through this typed IPC layer, the single most important seam in the app. ipc.ts routes every call across three interchangeable transports: Tauri IPC on the desktop, an HTTP backend on the web, and a mock for browser previews, so the exact same React build runs everywhere. vite.config.ts is the build that produces that frontend. Keep this seam in mind: every later backend command is reached through here.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript lets a single typed interface be backed by swappable implementations chosen at runtime. Here the transport tier (Tauri / HTTP / mock) is selected once behind one API surface, so platform differences never leak into the UI components that call it.

tour.title: Tauri Rust Backend Entry
tour.description: Cross the IPC seam from Step 4 and you land here, in native Rust. lib.rs is the Tauri application entry point: it builds the app, initializes shared AppState, and registers every IPC command handler exposed to the frontend. Cargo.toml declares the crate and its dependencies, and default.json is the capability manifest that grants each window permission to call those commands. This is the 'how does the backend start and what is it allowed to do?' layer.
tour.languageLesson: Tauri 2's capability model is allow-list security: a window can only invoke the commands its capability manifest grants. Registering a command in Rust is not enough — the JSON manifest must also permit the calling window, keeping the native surface tightly scoped.

tour.title: Connections & Query Execution
tour.description: These modules are the heart of the database client, sitting behind the commands registered in Step 5. connection.rs manages Exasol connections — pinging, building options, and opening sized pools. query.rs is the SQL execution engine that splits multi-statement scripts, runs them against the pool with row limits and timings, decodes result cells to JSON, and records history. catalog.rs introspects the live catalog to power schema graphs and object search. This is the path a query travels from editor to result grid.

tour.title: The Credential Vault
tour.description: Connections from Step 6 need secrets, and the app never stores them in the clear. security.rs implements the encrypted secret vault: key derivation from a master password, AEAD seal/open, unlock and password-change flows, recovery-code generation, and the encrypt/decrypt helpers that connection profiles rely on. This is the trust foundation that lets Studio hold database credentials safely on the user's machine.
tour.languageLesson: AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) both encrypts and authenticates: decryption fails loudly if the ciphertext was tampered with. Combined with key derivation from a master password, secrets are never persisted in plaintext and cannot be silently altered.

tour.title: Wiring In the AI Sidecar
tour.description: Studio's AI features are powered by a separate Node process, and these two files are the bridge to it. On the Rust side, agent.rs locates the bundled runtime, spawns the agent-core process, and exposes commands to grant it connections and proxy API/stream calls. On the frontend side, agent-client.ts proxies REST and SSE calls through those Rust commands to reach the sidecar's localhost server despite browser mixed-content restrictions. This is how the UI and the AI talk.

tour.title: Inside the Agent Core
tour.description: Now step into the sidecar itself. index.ts boots the process: it parses --data-dir, starts the config store and HTTP server, and prints a ready line the Rust side waits for. server.ts is the token-authenticated HTTP/WebSocket server wiring sessions, tools, MCP, and memory behind streaming turn execution. loop.ts is the agent turn engine that runs a full conversation turn with retrieval context, tool selection, and completion heuristics. This is the brain behind 'Exa', the in-app assistant.
tour.languageLesson: An agent loop repeatedly asks the model what to do, executes any tool calls it requests, feeds the results back, and continues until the model signals completion. loop.ts wraps that cycle with retrieval context and error-humanizing so a single user turn can span many model/tool round-trips.

tour.title: Tools, MCP, Memory & Skills
tour.description: The turn engine from Step 9 is only useful because of what the agent can do and remember. tools.ts is the central factory building every agent tool — SQL execution, filesystem, dashboards, exapump — bound to a runtime context. mcp.ts manages MCP connectors that expose external servers as additional tools. memory.ts embeds and recalls facts to inject relevant context into turns, and skills.ts stores reusable, recallable agent skills. Together they define the agent's capabilities and long-term knowledge.

tour.title: Assistant UI & Dashboards
tour.description: Back in the frontend, this is where the agent from Steps 8-10 becomes something a user interacts with. AssistantPanel.tsx is the chat panel handling message streaming, markdown and code rendering, tool-call views, permission prompts, and slash commands — the UI that shows every step and asks before changing anything. Dashboards.tsx is the BI feature that turns query results into KPI, chart, and table panels the agent can build on the user's behalf.

tour.title: The SQL Parser Package
tour.description: Whether a human or the agent writes SQL, this package makes the editor smart. ExasolParser.g4 and ExasolLexer.g4 are the ANTLR4 grammars defining Exasol SQL — including a lexer island mode that keeps embedded Python/Lua/Java/R script bodies opaque. completion.ts walks the parse tree to produce caret-aware suggestions and parse errors, and sql-completion.ts wires that engine into the Monaco editor with live-catalog awareness. This is the intelligence behind autocomplete and inline diagnostics.
tour.languageLesson: ANTLR generates a lexer and parser from .g4 grammar files; the antlr4-c3 code-completion engine then walks the parse tree at the cursor to compute which tokens are legal next. Routing identifiers through named rules (schemaName/tableName/columnName) is what lets completion know whether to suggest a schema, table, or column.

tour.title: The Semantic Views Layer
tour.description: The tour ends at the database-side foundation that makes plain-language questions answerable. 001_create_semantic_catalog.sql defines the 34-table SYS_SEMANTIC data model (models, entities, metrics, relationships, validation, audit). 002 projects those into stable public catalog views, and 006 builds the denormalized '..._FOR_AGENT' views the AI browses to understand the data. 005 provides publishing and preprocessor helpers, while sales_physical_model.sql is the demo star-schema those semantic models describe. This is how the agent maps 'revenue by region' to real tables.
tour.languageLesson: SQL views denormalize a normalized schema into a stable, query-friendly surface without duplicating data. Here the raw SYS_SEMANTIC tables stay normalized for integrity, while the layered CATALOG and FOR_AGENT views present an LLM-friendly shape — decoupling how data is stored from how the agent reads it.
